public_rationale: This forecast depends on a condition: that the io gadget is an always-worn device with a camera and microphone. As of October 2026, OpenAI had not announced or released any consumer device. In June 2025, an io co-founder told a court the first device would not be wearable. July 2026 reports described it as a home speaker that was still in development. Because no qualifying device exists, nobody can yet check whether it monitors users all the time or whether OpenAI trains on what it collects.
limitations: Device details come from news reports of court filings and anonymous sources, not released specs.
A later OpenAI device could still meet the condition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI's planned io gadget is, as it would seem, an always-worn device with a camera and microphone, its users would be monitored all the time, with everything they say and do recorded, analyzed, interpreted and turned into data that OpenAI trains its models on.
conditions: if the gadget is, as it would seem, worn all the time with a camera and microphone

statement.excerpt: A camera and microphone. You would be monitored all the time. Everything you say, everything you do, and not just recorded, but analyzed, interpreted and turned into data, which of course OpenAI train their models on.
statement.document_title: Black Mirror was a warmup act

from_speaker: The idea, it would seem, is ... a little AI-powered gadget that you wear all the time, maybe like a necklace or pendant
You would be monitored all the time
Everything you say, everything you do ... recorded, but analyzed, interpreted and turned into data
which of course OpenAI train their models on
our_interpretation: Read as a conditional forecast. Antecedent: OpenAI's io gadget turns out to be an always-worn device with a camera and microphone. Consequent: users are monitored continuously and OpenAI trains its models on the captured data.
Scoring needs the device to exist with that form, plus evidence about how it captures data and how that data is used.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI releases an always-worn io device with a camera and microphone, and specs, independent testing or OpenAI's data-use terms show it captures users' speech and actions continuously and that the data is used to train OpenAI models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Such a device is released, but it does not capture continuously (for example, it only listens on a wake word), or OpenAI does not use the data for training (for example, training is opt-in or excluded by default).

evidence.excerpt: Tan says the first device it plans to launch "is not an in-ear device, nor a wearable device."
evidence.explanation: io's co-founder told a court the first device would not be wearable. This weighs against the antecedent that the gadget is worn all the time.

evidence.excerpt: the device — which is still currently under development — is designed to be screen-free and is being pitched internally as a “humanlike AI companion that lives in the home.”
evidence.explanation: As of July 2026 the reported first device was an unreleased home speaker, not an always-worn pendant, so the antecedent had not been shown to hold.

evidence.excerpt: As of 16 October 2026, OpenAI’s own website (openai.com) still gives no launch date for a first consumer device and announces no such product
evidence.explanation: No OpenAI consumer device had been announced or released close to the evaluation date, so there is nothing yet to test the forecast on.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Release of an OpenAI always-worn device with a camera and microphone, plus its published data-use terms or independent testing showing whether it captures continuously and whether that data trains OpenAI models.
